issues.description: mmdet bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 without justification in PR title/description
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'Fix mmengine failure' but also upgrades mmdet from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0. This is an undocumented dependency change that could introduce behavioral differences or break compatibility with the pinned mmcv==2.1.0. Either justify the bump in the description or keep mmdet pinned at 3.2.0 to keep the fix minimal.

issues.description: Hard runtime cap of setuptools<82 in core/setup.py affects all downstream users, not just CI
issues.detail: Adding 'setuptools<82' to install_requires in core/setup.py constrains every user of autogluon.core, not only the CI environment that needs the cap for mmcv builds. This is a viral upper bound on a foundational build tool. The cap should live in the ray extras only, or in CI scripts, not in the base install_requires.

issues.description: mmcv install with --no-build-isolation may pick up host setuptools instead of the pinned one
issues.detail: Using '--no-build-isolation' means the build uses whatever setuptools is currently installed. The preceding 'pip install setuptools<82' tries to ensure this, but order/timing in CI venvs can still leave a newer setuptools resident. Worth a comment explaining the ordering invariant or verifying setuptools downgrade actually takes effect before the mmcv build.

issues.description: setuptools cap added without a tracking issue or removal trigger condition
issues.detail: The FIXME references open-mmlab/mmcv#3325 but core/setup.py has no comment linking to it. When mmcv fixes the issue, whoever revisits core/setup.py won't know why 'setuptools<82' is there. Add the same FIXME comment to core/setup.py line 63 so the cap can be removed in lockstep.

issues.description: mmengine pinned to 0.10.7 without explanation of why this version
issues.detail: Previously mmengine was installed from a specific git SHA chosen for a torch 2.5 fix. Switching to PyPI 0.10.7 should be checked: does 0.10.7 contain that same torch 2.5 fix? If not, the underlying problem the SHA pin solved may regress silently. Worth noting which release contains the fix.

review.summary: The PR works around the mmcv/setuptools>=82 incompatibility by capping setuptools and switching mmengine to a PyPI release, which is a reasonable CI fix. Main concerns: the setuptools<82 cap leaks into core/setup.py install_requires (affecting all downstream users, not just CI), mmdet was bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 without mention in the PR description, and the rationale for choosing mmengine 0.10.7 (vs the prior git SHA pinned for torch 2.5) is not documented. Suggest scoping the setuptools cap to CI or extras, justifying the mmdet bump, and cross-linking the FIXME tracker issue in core/setup.py.
